subject: Acme RAG eval - post-call recap & recommended next steps

Subject: Re: Acme RAG eval - discovery follow-up and next steps

Hi Sam / Emily —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our discovery call and proposed next steps so we keep momentum:

What I heard
- Goal: Improve internal support search + automated summary generation for long product docs so support agents get correct context in <10s.
- Primary constraints: low latency (p95 < 700ms for agent UI), strict grounding requirements (minimal hallucination), mix of private docs + public KB, and retention / auditability requirements.
- Data: ~500k docs (mix of short KB articles and long design docs). Currently using a basic keyword search + BM25.

High-level recommendation (RAG path)
1) Retriever: Hybrid dense + sparse. Run dense embeddings (256-d) for semantic recall + BM25 for keyword precision. We recommend starting with a FAISS HNSW index for vectors and enabling BM25 hybrid recall as a filter.
2) Reranker: Two-stage approach. Candidate retriever returns top-50, then a lightweight cross-encoder reranker for top-5 to maximize grounding. Tradeoffs: cross-encoder gives best precision but adds latency; we suggest a quantized cross-encoder (cpu or small-gpu) to keep p95 under target.
3) Generator/model: Evaluate two model families for your workload: a smaller, faster model for interactive agent UI (redwood-7b-quant or a 13B quantized variant) and a higher-quality model for long-form summaries (redwood-13b-instruct or Llama-2-Chat-70B if you want max quality). We'll run both in our eval harness and expose latency/grounding metrics.

Metrics we'll track in the eval
- Precision@k (for retrieval), Recall@k, and R-precision
- Grounding rate (percent of model-generated assertions that cite at least one retrieved doc)
- Hallucination rate measured against the QA reference set (binary correct/incorrect per answer)
- Latency p50/p95 for both retrieval+rerank and end-to-end generation
- Cost per query (tokens + infra)

Immediate next steps
- I'll share a short eval plan and a sample prompt set (attached). Please confirm data access method: S3 read role or shared signed URLs? We also need a representative QA prompt set (10-20 seed examples) for early regression checks.
- Proposed timeline: 2-week eval run (week 1: retrieval + reranker sweep; week 2: model A/B and prompt tuning).
- Follow-up call: propose Tue 20 Apr 10:00am PT for a quick checkpoint and to review first-run metrics.

Attachments: acme_rag_eval_plan.pdf (plan + metrics), acme_sample_prompts.csv (seed prompts + expected answers)

If that matches your expectation I’ll request S3 access and kick off the eval.

—Marissa

Adding some technical detail on the reranker + latency tradeoffs — hi Sam,

Short answers:
- Cross-encoder latency: for a quantized cross-encoder reranker (e.g., crossenc-bert-6B-quant) we typically see ~60-90ms per candidate on a modern GPU. If we rerank top-50 it's too slow; the pattern we use is: dense retriever -> top-50 -> lightweight bi-encoder quick-re-rank to top-10 -> cross-encoder on top-5. That keeps additional rerank latency in the ~120-220ms range on a single GPU.
- End-to-end: with HNSW retrieval (~30-60ms depending on doc size) + the rerank path above + redwood-7b-quant generation (~200-350ms for short responses) you should expect p95 in the ~450-650ms window, assuming well-tuned batching.

We’ll include a latency breakdown in the first run so you can see per-component p50/p95. For grounding/citations: we’ll instrument the generator to surface token-level provenance for any cited passages and compute percent of claims that have at least one supporting doc in the retrieval set. That metric is what we call "grounding rate" in the report.

On privacy/transfer: S3 role is fine. If you need us to run inside your VPC for the eval (private deployment), we can propose a dedicated short-lived private run; that will add 2-3 days for provisioning.

I’ll prepare a reranker sweep plan (bi-encoder candidates for recall, cross-encoder variants for precision) and include suggested hyperparameters (score thresholds, top-k values) in the eval plan.

-Rishi
